•  The benzene ring shown by the spectrum is tetrasubstituted (only two different aromatic-H signals).  
  A benzene ring accounts for 4 degrees of unsaturation (DU = rings + π-bonds).

•  FT-IR shows an ester C=O, which adds 1 DU.  
  The 1H-NMR shows two nonequivalent vinylic protons (one d, one dq) ⇒ there is an extra C=C bond outside the ring, adding 1 more DU.

  Total DU required = 4 (benzene) + 1 (C=O) + 1 (C=C) = 6.

•  Calculate DU (= C – H/2 + 1) for the candidate formulas:  
  – C11H12O2: 11 – 12/2 + 1 = 6  
  – C11H14O2: 11 – 14/2 + 1 = 5  
  – C12H12O2: 12 – 12/2 + 1 = 7  
  – C12H14O2: 12 – 14/2 + 1 = 6

  Only C11H12O2 and C12H14O2 have DU = 6.

•  Proton count from NMR signals:  
  2 aromatic H (but each signal integrates to 2H) → 4 H  
  2 vinylic H → 2 H  
  2 CH3 groups → 6 H  
  Total = 12 H

  Therefore the molecule must contain 12 hydrogens, ruling out C12H14O2 (14 H).  
  Moreover, no CH2 signal is present; C12H14O2 would require an extra –CH2– or additional CH protons, contradicting the spectrum.

Hence the only formula consistent with both the degrees of unsaturation and the proton count is:

Answer: C
